title: Eddington: the background of the pointer readings is of a spiritual nature

statements.text: Since the schedule of pointer readings is attached to some unknown background, Eddington proposed attaching it to something of a spiritual nature whose prominent characteristic is thought, rather than to a concrete nature inconsistent with thought. For the readings of his own brain he has an insight beyond the readings, and he expects the background elsewhere to be continuous with it, without always having the more specialized attributes of consciousness.

sources.quote: Why not then attach it to something of spiritual nature of which a prominent characteristic is thought.
It seems rather silly to prefer to attach it to something of a so-called "concrete" nature inconsistent with thought, and then to wonder where the thought comes from.
Although I may expect that the background of other pointer readings in physics is of a nature continuous with that revealed to me in this particular case
